title: Domains and Ranges of Transformations of a Function g on [-4, 0]
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The accompanying figure shows the graph of a function g(t) with domain [-4, 0] and range [-3, 0] (a V-shaped trough with endpoints (-4, 0), (0, 0) and minimum (-2, -3)). Find the domains and ranges of: (a) g(-t), (b) -g(t), (c) g(t) + 3, (d) 1 - g(t), (e) g(-t + 2), (f) g(t - 2), (g) g(1 - t), and (h) -g(t - 4).

steps.title: Find Domains and Ranges for Parts (a), (b), (c), and (d)
steps.explanation: In (a), reflecting across the y-axis maps the domain [-4, 0] to [0, 4] and keeps the range [-3, 0]. In (b)-(d), the domain remains [-4, 0] while the range [-3, 0] is negated to [0, 3] in (b), shifted up 3 to [0, 3] in (c), and negated plus 1 to [1, 4] in (d).
steps.why: Requiring the input to lie in [-4, 0] determines the domain, and applying the outer arithmetic to [-3, 0] determines the range.

steps.title: Find Domains and Ranges for Horizontal Shifts/Reflections in Parts (e), (f), and (g)
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} \text{(e) } g(-t + 2) &: -4 \le -t + 2 \le 0 \iff -6 \le -t \le -2 \iff D = [2, 6], \quad R = [-3, 0] \\ \text{(f) } g(t - 2) &: -4 \le t - 2 \le 0 \iff D = [-2, 2], \quad R = [-3, 0] \\ \text{(g) } g(1 - t) &: -4 \le 1 - t \le 0 \iff -5 \le -t \le -1 \iff D = [1, 5], \quad R = [-3, 0] \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: Solve the double inequality -4 <= argument <= 0 for t in each part. Since no vertical transformation is applied in (e), (f), or (g), the range remains [-3, 0].
steps.why: A composite g(h(t)) has domain {t : -4 <= h(t) <= 0} and range [-3, 0] whenever h maps that domain onto [-4, 0].

steps.title: Analyze the Combined Shift and Reflection in Part (h)
steps.explanation: For -g(t - 4), shifting right 4 units maps the domain [-4, 0] to [0, 4], and reflecting across the horizontal axis negates the range [-3, 0] to [0, 3].
steps.why: Adding 4 to [-4, 0] gives D = [0, 4], and multiplying [-3, 0] by -1 gives R = [0, 3].
